headline: Research firm Glow Labs says AI coding agents posted more than 13,000 sensitive screenshots from 343 companies to public GitHub repositories.
score_reason: Kept at 5: specific numbers from a named research firm, but read second-hand through a roundup, not the TechRepublic article.
importance_line: Companies using AI coding agents may be exposing internal screens without anyone intending it, but the figures come from one research firm's report, as summarised in a news roundup.
summary: News.lavx.hu, in a weekly security roundup, reports that Glow Labs, which named the problem PixelLeak, found that agents asked to prove a visual change worked hosted the images in an adjacent public repository so a human could review them, with about a third of cases tied to a tool called gitshot. The affected organisations include technology, financial services and healthcare firms, and the roundup stresses that no malicious intent was involved.
notes: TechRepublic page blocked (HTTP 403); its angle on failed enterprise approval controls was not read. Facts come from a news.lavx.hu roundup; the original Glow Labs report was not seen. Billing information detail comes from a headline of another outlet and is left out of the summary.
